captions.detailed: This 3D model presents a two-part sewable button battery holder, consisting of a top cap and a bottom cup. The bottom cup features a circular recess to contain the battery, surrounded by small external mounting loops (sew holes) distributed around its perimeter. The flat top cap includes mating clips on its outer edge to snap securely over the bottom cup, along with its own set of sew loops. Both parts feature central cutouts and small wire holes to route electrical connections directly to the battery terminals.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric, sewable button battery clip holder in OpenSCAD consisting of a top cap and a bottom section. The script should support standard battery sizes like CR2032 and AG13, or custom dimensions, and include options to adjust the radius of the sew holes, edge thickness, and whether to include sew holes on the top cap.
captions.factory: The code defines two primary modules: 'bottomsection' and 'topsection'. The 'bottomsection' utilizes a 'divider' module built from nested cylinders and subtracted cubes for wire routing, surrounded by a loop of small cylinders with subtracted inner cylinders for the sew holes. The 'topsection' uses a reversed cylinder base with snapping clips generated by the 'clip' module (constructed using translated cubes arranged with a for-loop), and optionally adds sewing rings. Custom text is engraved on the top cap using an imported 8-bit polyfont library and 'linear_extrude' with 'polygon' paths.
